senses.gloss: [also ָה, a. with one ו] m. (Ispe. noun of סב, סבב = h. אִיסְטֵיב q. v., b. h. מֵסֵב; v. אִיסְ־) a surrounding, attachment, whence
balcony, colonnade, portico (also an independent colonnade), esp. הָאִ׳ the Itst’ba (Ist’ba) the Temple portico.
units: <cite ref="Mishnah Pesachim 1:5">Pes. I, 5</cite> (<cite ref="Pesachim 11b">11ᵇ</cite>) <he>על גג האיצ׳</he> Ms. M. (Bab. ed. incorr. <he>גב</he>, Var. <cite ref="A01421"><he>אִסְטְוָה</he></cite>, v. Rabb. D. S. a. l. note). Ib. 13ᵇ one recited <he>על גב</he> on top (inside) …, say <he>על גג הא׳</he> on the roof of the Its. (so as to expose it to public view). Y. Sabb. I, 2ᵈ bot. <he>איסטוה וכ׳</he>; Bab.

<cite ref="Shabbat 7a:4">Sabb. 7ᵃ</cite> <he>איצ׳ שלפני העמודים</he> a balcony in front of the columns (projecting into the street, used as a stand for dealers, v. <cite ref="A01433"><he>אִיסְטֵיב</he></cite>).
<cite ref="Shabbat 7a">Ib.</cite> <he>דוקא א׳ דלא ניחא תשמישיה</he> Ms. M. (ed. <he>א׳ הוא דלא</he>) only the colonnade the use of which for passers by is not convenient.

<cite ref="Bamidbar Rabbah 12">Num. R. s. 12</cite> two columns of silver which were placed in front of the Ark <he>כמין איסטווה</he> (<cite ref="Shir HaShirim Rabbah 1:11">Cant. R. to I, 11</cite> <he>אִיסְטְוִוין</he> pl.) forming a kind of balcony; <cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Sotah 8:3:8">Y. Sot. VIII, 22ᶜ</cite> <he>תנם לא׳</he> allow the surplus of three handbreadths (over the space occupied by the Tablets) for the balcony.—
<cite ref="Yoma 49a:4">Yoma 49ᵃ</cite> <he>דעבוד מעשה אסטווה</he> Ar. (ed. <he>איצ׳</he>) they (the laymen) served only the purpose of a portico (holding the bowls up to view, v.
<cite ref="Mishnah Pesachim 1:5">Pes. I, 5</cite>, but not handing them to the altar).—
<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Sukkah 5:1:4">Y. Succ. V, 55ᵃ</cite> bot., v. <cite ref="D00679"><he>דִּיפְּלֵי</he></cite>.

senses.gloss: (cmp. הֶסֵּב, הֲסִיבָּה) something to recline on; couch, seat.
units: <cite ref="Kiddushin 70a:15">Kidd. 70ᵃ</cite>, (to one using the high-toned <he>קרפיטא</he> q. v.) <he>א׳ דאמרי אינשי</he> call it itst’ba as the people do.—

M. Kat. 10ᵇ למבני א׳ Ar. a. ed. (Var. as Yoma l. c.) to build a temporary banqueting place for guests during the festive week, cmp. אַכְוַרְנְקָא, (Rashi: stone building, Ms. Rashi כסא).—Pl. אִיצְטְבָאוֹת (h. form).

<cite ref="Pesachim 65b:6">Pes. 65ᵇ</cite> <he>דמסגי אא׳</he> they (the priests) walked alongside the walls on balconies (projecting boards made for them that they should not tread on the blood); Y. ib. V, 32ᶜ bot. <he>מִסְטְוָיוֹת</he>, V. <he>מִסְטְוָה</he>.
